name: The Drowned Grove
_design: One room, off the route, that answers a question the player has not asked yet: why is Mirehaven on stilts? Because there is a Mirehaven under the water, and half of one roof is still above it. Nothing here says so. There is no sign, no NPC and no cutscene -- there is a thatched gable standing in four feet of marsh with a door in it that does not open, and a player who walks in here and works it out has been told the second truth of this act in miniature before the Sanctum says it out loud.
_plan: Dark, and lit entirely by glowcaps. It is the only place in the game that is both -- caves are dark and unlit, towns are lit and not dark -- and the eighteen caps are placed as a ring round the bowl rather than scattered, so the room reads as a lamplit hall the moment the player steps in. The fog is thinned to a third of the route's, because the canopy is shut over it: walking in here is the fog LIFTING, which is the only relief the region gives, and it lands in the one room built out of somebody's drowned house.

text: A door, in a wall, in the water. The thatch above it is three winters gone
and still holding. The sill is eleven inches under and the latch still works.
It opens onto the rest of the house, and the rest of the house is not here.
A punt, swamped, tied to a pile with a knot somebody expected to untie.
Whatever they came back for, they did not come back for the boat.
A pile, cut off level with the water and worn round on top.
There are more of them under the surface. You can feel them through your boots
for eleven paces in every direction, which is about the size of a street.
